stage_2_story.text_en:
Ilan had not spoken to his neighbour, Mr Greenberg, in over a year. They had argued about a parking space and things had been cold between them ever since. Ilan's wife kept saying, 'You need to break the ice before you burn your bridges completely.'

One morning, Ilan saw Mr Greenberg struggling with heavy shopping bags in the hallway. He decided to bite the bullet and offered to help. Mr Greenberg looked surprised but said, 'Thank you — I am feeling a bit under the weather today.'

They walked inside together and Ilan helped carry the bags to the kitchen. It felt a little awkward at first, but once they started talking about their families, the conversation flowed. Mr Greenberg even made coffee and they sat down for half an hour.

'I have to say,' said Mr Greenberg, 'you hit the nail on the head when you said the parking problem was about respect, not just space. I think I overreacted.'

Ilan smiled. He felt it was a piece of cake to forgive someone once you really talked to them. He also mentioned that he was going to the hardware store and offered to pick up some items for Mr Greenberg too — kill two birds with one stone.

They shook hands at the door. Ilan thought: the repair that costs an arm and a leg is not the parking lot — it is the damage you do to a friendship.
